overview: An indemnification clause allocates legal and financial risk between Landlord and Tenant for third-party claims arising from use of the Premises. A typical clause contains: (a) Tenant's obligation to indemnify Landlord for claims arising from Tenant's use, occupancy, or acts/omissions of its agents, and (b) often, Landlord's reciprocal obligation to indemnify Tenant for claims arising from Landlord's negligence or willful misconduct. The clause works in tandem with the parties' insurance obligations — in most cases the indemnitor's insurance is the first source of recovery.

General Applicability: All leases (Office, Retail and Industrial).

questions.question_text: Does the lease contain indemnification obligations?
questions.extraction_hint: Extract the full indemnification clause(s), identifying separately: (a) Tenant-indemnifies-Landlord, (b) Landlord-indemnifies-Tenant (if mutual), (c) any carve-outs or exclusions.
questions.red_flag: Flag if Tenant indemnifies Landlord for Landlord's own negligence (unusual and unfavorable to Tenant).

questions.question_text: Is the indemnification mutual (both parties indemnify each other)?
questions.extraction_hint: Determine if Landlord also indemnifies Tenant. If yes, extract the Landlord-to-Tenant indemnity.
